title: The Curta pocket calculator was drawn up by a prisoner in Buchenwald

cover.alt: A Curta Type I: a small black cylinder with a crank on top and number sliders down its side, a little like a pepper grinder.
cover.credit: Rama, Musée des Arts et Métiers · CC BY-SA 3.0 fr

body: The Austrian engineer **Curt Herzstark** conceived a palm-sized mechanical calculator in Vienna in the 1930s, and in 1938 patented its key trick: a single stepped drum that can subtract by adding complements. In 1943 Herzstark, whose father was Jewish, was sent to Buchenwald concentration camp. There he was encouraged to keep working on the calculator; a camp official reportedly told him that if it was worth something, it would be given to Hitler as a present after the war was won. After US troops liberated the camp in April 1945, he found a factory near Weimar by November to build three working prototypes. From 1948 the **Curta** was made in Liechtenstein, and it stayed in production until 1972.

slides.heading: Subtracting by adding
slides.text: Calculators of the day typically used around ten stepped drums. Herzstark used one, and it also subtracts by adding nines' complements, a disguised version of the number, which avoids the fiddly gearing of borrowing. That single drum was the key to shrinking the machine to palm size.

slides.heading: Type I or Type II?
slides.explanation: The bigger Type II, from 1954, set 11 digits and gave 15-digit results. The original Type I set 8 and gave 11.

slides.heading: Curtas made, 1948 to 1972
slides.note: About 140,000 in all, made by Contina AG in Mauren, Liechtenstein.

events.text: The Type I goes on sale

slides.heading: Built for bumpy roads
slides.text: Rally navigators used Curtas from the 1960s into the 1980s for time-speed-distance events, because early electronic calculators coped badly with the jolts. Pilots used them for weight-and-balance sums. Until electronic calculators took over in the 1970s, it was considered the best portable calculator there was.

slides.question: How do you switch a Curta from adding to subtracting?
slides.explanation: Pulling the crank up slightly before turning it makes the Curta subtract instead of add.
